title: beta→GA昇格やSDK major更新で、呼び出し側を変更していないAPIの破壊範囲・必須引数が黙って変わる
summary: When a provider graduates an API out of beta or ships an SDK major version, call sites that did not change can change meaning. On 2026-08-27 Anthropic unified the beta and stable SDK namespaces, and client.beta.skills.delete() went from deleting one Skill to deleting 'a Skill together with all of its versions'; BetaSkill was renamed BetaContainerSkill. On 2026-08-20 Python SDK v1.0 removed temperature, top_p and top_k from Messages methods and made AnthropicBedrock error rather than default to us-east-1. The diff at the call site is empty, so neither code review nor an AI-driven dependency upgrade sees anything to flag - the widened blast radius surfaces only at runtime, on real data.

evidence.title: Claude Platform release notes, 2026-08-27
evidence.summary: 'client.beta.files and client.beta.skills no longer send the files-api-2025-04-14 and skills-2025-10-02 beta headers and return the same shapes as client.files and client.skills. With this change, client.beta.skills.delete() deletes a Skill together with all of its versions, and the beta Messages type BetaSkill ... is renamed BetaContainerSkill.'

evidence.title: Claude Platform release notes, 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-19
evidence.summary: Python SDK v1.0 removes temperature/top_p/top_k on Messages methods and the legacy Text Completions API; AnthropicBedrock raises instead of defaulting to us-east-1. Separately, computer use leaving beta means 'Upgrading an existing integration changes the request shape and tool handling'.

notes: Checked E08 (dependency/migration changes included carelessly by AI), C06 (stale API knowledge), I04 (destructive command from misinference). E08 is about the AI adding an unrequested upgrade; C06 is about the AI using outdated knowledge. Neither covers 'the same unchanged call now destroys more', which is invisible to diff-based review and is the specific hazard when an agent performs the upgrade. Lower confidence because the observed instance is single-vendor.
